first.rationale: Current decline in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ) suggests friction in the product experience post-signup. Memory_91 demonstrated that activation messaging improved week-one engagement and drove first meaningful actions—directly addressing the activation dip. Memory_86 showed onboarding improvements lift early adoption. Before committing, verifying memory_31 (signup simplification) and memory_91 (activation messaging) will clarify whether the activation decline stems from upstream friction (signup barriers) or downstream disengagement (in-product messaging gaps). Activation messaging is lower-risk than promotional pricing (which trains price sensitivity in the SMB segment we're losing to competitor pricing) and enterprise_sales_assist (which requires sales capacity allocation). A standard experiment on activation messaging targets the immediate QoQ decline while preserving the option to layer on pricing strategies or sales support if activation messaging alone proves insufficient.
